lesson_title: The Goat, the Wheel and the Road: Circles and Tangents
hook_text: A goat on a 5-metre rope and a bicycle wheel on flat tar — together they answer the two hardest-looking questions in analytical geometry.
clip_script: Tie a goat to a peg with a taut 5-metre rope and walk it all the way around. The path it traces is every point exactly 5 from the peg — a circle, and its equation is just the distance formula: x minus a squared, plus y minus b squared, equals r squared. Reading one is two questions. What kills each bracket? That is the centre — x minus 3 means the peg stands at positive 3. What is the root of the right side? That is the rope — 25 stores a radius of 5. Now the wheel. A bicycle wheel kisses the tar at exactly one point, and the spoke to that point stands dead square to the road. Centre, radius, tangent — and square means gradients multiplying to minus 1. So the tangent at any point costs four small steps: confirm the point is on the circle, take the spoke's gradient with rise over run, flip it and negate it, and write the line through the point. Substitute the point back, watch it balance, done. One goat, one wheel, full marks.
visual_style: A goat circling a wooden peg on green veld, its path burning into a clean coordinate-grid circle, then a bicycle wheel rolling in with one glowing spoke snapping perpendicular to the road at the kiss point.
mood: Warm, rural, quietly precise — farm picture turning into exam machinery.
pacing: A gentle circular sweep with the goat, two crisp reading questions, then four quick beats through the tangent steps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any circle equation at a glance.
